        Frequently asked questions
        
        
        How the generator works and what to do if the tunnel does not come up.
        
        
        
          
        
            What is AmneziaWG and how is it different from WireGuard?
            
        AmneziaWG is a WireGuard fork by the Amnezia team. Encryption and keys are the same as in WireGuard, but the protocol adds obfuscation: junk packets before the handshake (Jc, Jmin, Jmax), CPS imitation packets (I1–I5) and, from AWG 2.0 on, header and padding parameters. This makes AmneziaWG traffic harder to identify by the WireGuard signature.
        
          
        
          
        
            What is Cloudflare WARP and do I need my own server?
            
        WARP is a free Cloudflare service built on WireGuard. The generator registers a new device through the official WARP API and builds a ready config from the result, so no server of your own is needed. The Cloudflare server stays a standard WireGuard peer, which is why some AmneziaWG parameters are intentionally fixed for it: S1–S4 = 0, H1–H4 = 1–4, MTU 1280.
        
          
        
          
        
            Which profile should I choose: AWG 1.5, 2.0, 3.0 or 3.1?
            
        Start with AWG 2.0: it is the default and imports into current AmneziaWG and AmneziaVPN. AWG 1.5 is for older clients. AWG 3.0 and 3.1 add client-side features of newer versions such as timing randomization; 3.1 needs AmneziaVPN 5.0.1.5+ or a compatible client. If the import fails, go back to AWG 2.0.
        
          
        
          
        
            How do I import the config into AmneziaWG or AmneziaVPN?
            
        On Windows, install the AmneziaWG client and add a tunnel from the downloaded .conf file. On Android and iOS, use AmneziaVPN or AmneziaWG: import the .conf file or paste the vpn:// link if it is available for the chosen profile. For routers (Keenetic, OpenWrt, MikroTik, GL.iNet), turn on "Router mode" in settings before generating.
        
          
        
          
        
            The config imports but does not connect. What should I do?
            
        Try another UDP port (2408, 500, 1701) and an endpoint IP address instead of the hostname — both are in the settings of step 2. On mobile networks, turn on the mobile profile. Make sure your client version supports the chosen AWG profile. If it connects but sites do not open, check DNS and routes. The current service state is on the Status page.
        
          
        
          
        
            Is it free? What happens to the keys?
            
        The generator is free and needs no sign-up. Keys are created during generation and handed straight to you — the server does not store them. Generation history is kept only in your browser and can be cleared. The source code is open under the AGPL-3.0 license.
        
          
        
          
        
            Can I route only some sites through WARP?
            
        Yes. In settings, choose split routing and tick the services you need: only their IPv4 subnets go into AllowedIPs, and other traffic goes directly. To keep the config reliable on phones and routers, the generator limits the list to 1000 IPv4 subnets.

        What to check if it does not work
        
            
          
              
        • If it does not connect: check endpoint, port, UDP availability, AWG mode, and client version.
          • 
              
        • If it connects but websites do not open: check DNS, AllowedIPs, IPv6, and MTU.
          • 
              
        • If it works on Wi-Fi but not on mobile network: try another port, hostname instead of IP, or another endpoint mode.
          • 
              
        • If import fails: check the AWG mode, client parser version, profile format, and import method. AWG 3.0 vpn:// is intentionally unavailable.
          •

        Additional Information
        
            
        Routes, AWG versions and Cloudflare peer limits
        
          
        
          
        
        
        
        
          
        
            
        Routes and AllowedIPs
        
            
        By default, all traffic goes through the tunnel (AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0). In settings (step 2) you can choose a DNS server and presets — only the required IPv4 subnets will be routed through the tunnel. IPv6 can be enabled optionally, but it increases the route count 2–3× and may cause issues on routers and mobile clients. Safe limit — 1000 IPv4 CIDR.
        
            
        IP ranges can be replaced manually. Up-to-date lists at opencck.org and rockblack.pro.
        
          
        

          
        
            
        
              
        AWG 1.5 Legacy
        
              
          
                
        • Static obfuscation parameters (Jc, S1–S4, H1–H4)
          • 
                
        • Masks only the start of the connection
          • 
                
        • Works with Cloudflare WARP without a server
          • 
                
        • Compatible with older clients
          • 
              
        
            
        
            
        
              
        AWG 2.0 client config
        
              
          
                
        • Dynamic headers + random padding in all packets
          • 
                
        • Mimics QUIC/DNS throughout the entire session
          • 
                
        • Harder to detect with heuristic DPI analysis
          • 
                
        • Requires client ≥ 4.8.12.9 (Amnezia)
          • 
              
        
            
        
            
        
              
        AWG 3.0 WARP-safe
        
              
          
                
        • Timing randomization and a PersistentKeepalive range
          • 
                
        • Client-side mechanisms only — the Cloudflare peer stays standard
          • 
                
        • Requires a client that supports AWG 3.x parameters
          • 
              
        
            
        
            
        
              
        AWG 3.1 WARP-safe
        
              
          
                
        • Everything in AWG 3.0 plus new 3.1 client features
          • 
                
        • AmneziaVPN 5.0.1.5+ or a compatible AWG 3.1 client is recommended
          • 
                
        • If import fails, choose AWG 2.0
          • 
              
        
            
        
          
        

          
        
            
        Is a server required for AWG 2.0?
        
            
        For Cloudflare WARP — no. Configs from this generator work with Cloudflare's public server without any server-side configuration.
        
            
        For your own server — yes. Self-hosted AWG 2.0 requires an updated kernel/module amneziawg-linux-kernel-module on the server and new client configs (old AWG 1.5 configs become incompatible). See the official documentation for details.

        Install and import
        
          
          
            
        1. Download and install AmneziaWG:
          Follow the download link and get the installer for Windows. Install to the default path "C:\Program Files\...".
          2. 
            
        2. Generate and import the config file:
          Choose AWG 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, or 3.1 according to client support. AWG 3.x uses a WARP-safe client profile; AWG 3.1 is recommended with AmneziaVPN 5.0.1.5+ or a compatible client. Download the configuration and import the .conf file into the client.
          3. 
          
        
          
        After importing, enable the tunnel in the client. The client restores its state when Windows starts.
        

          
        
            What is this?
            
        
              
        The generator creates a ready AmneziaWG/WARP profile for import into a VPN client. You can download a .conf file or copy vpn:// if your client supports quick import. Full tunnel routes all supported traffic through WARP, while split tunnel routes only selected destinations. Connectivity depends on the client, network, endpoint, DNS, and routes.
        
              
        The generator reduces manual configuration, but it does not guarantee connectivity in every network or client.
        
            
        
          
        
        
        
      
        
    
        

    
    
        
      
        
        
        
          
          
        
            
        Privacy
        
            
        What happens to data during generation
        
          
        
          
        
        
        
        The awgconfig.com server registers a Cloudflare WARP device for you and immediately returns the finished config. Keys and configs are not stored on the server; only technical errors reach the logs.
        Generation history is kept only in this browser (localStorage) — you can clear it in the History window.
        Analytics: Yandex Metrica without Webvisor plus anonymous product events (mode, generation outcome). Keys, endpoint addresses and config contents are never sent to analytics.
        Third-party services: Cloudflare (WARP registration) and iplist.opencck.org (route lists for split tunnelling).
